posts.text:
No parent should have to spend the time after childbirth worrying about whether they will have their job once their baby comes home.

Today, I was joined by NICU parents and advocates to proudly introduce the Stand By NICU Babies and Families Act, which will ensure every parent https://t.co/57vCwvSlXw

When your newborn is in the NICU, the last thing any parent should worry about is losing their job—or using all their parental leave before their baby can even leave the hospital.

I just introduced the bipartisan Stand By NICU Babies and Families Act to give eligible parents up to 12 extra weeks of job-protected FMLA leave during a NICU stay, in addition to regular parental leave. Colorado showed this works—now it's time to deliver for families nationwide. Because when your baby is fighting for their life, the only thing that should matter is being there with them.
https://t.co/Hxdq2B5vrR

For so many families, pregnancy loss is a quiet, devastating heartbreak. 

The last thing anyone in that position needs is the threat of criminalization hanging over them. I'm proud to co-lead the Pregnancy Loss Protection Act to stand with women in Colorado and across the country, ensuring they are met with empathy and care.

Our veterans put everything on the line for our country, and we owe it to them to make sure they never have to fight alone for the care and benefits they earned.

As Trump and Republicans gut the VA, so many veterans are being left behind. But we won't let it happen. I signed a petition to force a vote on the Major Richard Star Act so combat-wounded veterans get their full retirement and disability benefits, and I fought to open a Fremont County VA clinic to serve over 5,000 veterans in our district.

If you or a veteran in your life needs help navigating the VA or accessing benefits, please reach out to my office at https://t.co/O8ThqKsfrd

Today and every day, thank you to our veterans!

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
